A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PACS. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–E are readable and matchable despite pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original PACS training and evaluation results, including mathematical reasoning benchmarks, ablations, cross-domain evaluations, and diversity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds a continuous-reward experiment in Section 6.3 and Table 4.

M1.justification: Section 6.3 adds a continuous-reward adaptation: learned scalar rewards are group-normalized to [0,1] and used as soft targets. The original binary-reward procedure, RLOO score function, cross-entropy objective, and reference-policy resets are retained.

E1.justification: v3 adds the training task of learning a continuous reward model from DeepScaleR-derived preference pairs. Existing mathematical reasoning, coding, and science evaluation coverage is retained; the continuous-reward evaluation reuses four existing math benchmarks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained experiments. The new Table 4 uses GRPO under continuous reward-model supervision; GRPO(RM) changes the reward setting of an existing comparator rather than introducing a new comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: Section 6.3 introduces a protocol using a Qwen3-8B reward model, Qwen3-4B policies, matched continuous-reward supervision, and pass@1 evaluation. Existing training budgets, inference settings, and the 128-candidate evaluation procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 adds an empirical test of PACS's effectiveness with learned continuous feedback. The earlier beta, score-function, and weighting ablations, cross-domain tests, and entropy/PCA diversity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The pass@k estimation procedure and candidate count are unchanged. No new seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced; Table 4 adds point accuracies without additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports PACS(RM) versus GRPO(RM) pass@1: 85.15 versus 83.91 on AMC23, 53.30 versus 52.84 on AIME2024, 40.91 versus 37.08 on AIME2025, and 26.84 versus 24.92 on BeyondAIME. These are additional results under continuous supervision; retained results, including appendix tables, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 adds an all-zero-reward specialization of the gradient and an argument that PACS continues updating when group-based advantages vanish. The existing mathematical formulation and Appendix A propositions and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about supervised RLVR reformulation, implicit actor–critic coupling, reasoning performance, and entropy preservation. The shortened abstract opening does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation of learning from uniform-reward groups and interprets the continuous-reward results as evidence of better use of fine-grained feedback and potential general RLHF applicability. The new study is described as preliminary; earlier interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 6.3 identifies the reward-model base, preference-data provenance, policy size, and reward normalization approach. Preference-pair construction, the normalization formula, and reward-model training hyperparameters remain unspecified. Existing Appendix C settings and code/data access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al. (2026), Learning ordinal probabilistic reward from preferences, in the continuous-reward discussion. Other reference changes largely update metadata for existing works, including the Gemini and OpenAI o1 references; the related-work framing is retained.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the abstract opening, expands the loss discussion, and adds Section 6.3, acknowledgements, and an impact statement. Authors and affiliations are updated, and bibliographic entries are expanded. Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 4 and rearranges Figure 3 from four horizontal panels into a 2-by-2 display beside Figure 4. The cross-domain and diversity figures exchange numbering and placement, and appendix tables are repaginated. These are localized presentation changes.

improvement.justification: Section 6.3 and Table 4 modestly strengthen the paper by adding a matched PACS–GRPO comparison under learned continuous rewards, extending v2's binary-reward training evidence while preserving earlier findings. The benefit is limited by incomplete reward-model training and normalization details, unchanged uncertainty reporting, and the absence of direct evaluation of general RLHF applicability.
